![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14096038/assets/5746a438eccdd55d345f1c71a768f971aa1a342798743e151f7557102ddd8783.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(1,-3).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(1,-3),$ we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=-3$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ (-3)^{2} & =4p(1) \\ 9 & =4p \\ p & =\frac{9}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{9}{4})x \\ {y}^{2} & =9x.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=\frac{9}{4}$ is positive.

question.knowledge_point: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm
question.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3x}\cdot 3\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{9\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}}{x}\,\text{d}x & =9\int \sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =9\int \sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =9\int {u}^{1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =9\cdot \frac{2{u}^{3/2}}{3}+C \\  & =6{u}^{3/2}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{{ln}^{3}⁡(3x)}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Describe the set of points shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
\{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,{{field-2}}\le x\le {{field-3}},\,{{field-4}}\le y\le {{field-5}}\}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in Z,y\in Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in Z\times Z={Z}^{2}.
$$

The points $P(x,y)$ satisfy the condition

$$
x\in \{-1,0,1,2\},\,y\in \{-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}.
$$

In other words,

$$
-1\le x\le 2,\,-2\le y\le 3.
$$

Therefore, we can write our set as follows:

$$
\{(x,y)\in {Z}^{2}\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,-2\le y\le 3\}
$$
